title: Pi Trainer user walkthrough
text: Welcome to Pi Trainer. This walkthrough takes you from a dataset to a model prepared for Raspberry Pi deployment. Training runs on your Mac, Windows computer, Linux machine, or a configured worker. The Raspberry Pi runs inference. We will use a small colour classification example to demonstrate the process. The accompanying guide contains installation commands, detailed specifications, and troubleshooting steps.

title: Create your project
text: Start the workbench using the web command in the guide, or launch the native desktop application. Both use the same project store when you select the same data directory. In the web interface, give the project a clear name. Select the exact accelerator you will deploy to: Hailo-8L, Hailo-8, or Hailo-10H. Choose computer vision, then create the project. Language model projects require the Hailo-10H target.

title: Import and version your data
text: Select the project before importing data. For image classification, organise your images into one folder per class, then enter that folder's path in Local dataset path. Import dataset creates a snapshot and records the files and their hashes. Our example contains red and blue images. For your own project, include realistic variation and keep related images from the same source together. Use the dataset workspace to upload files or save versioned labels and groups. Keep test data separate from training and calibration data.

title: Run and inspect training
text: Scroll to Train, build and deploy. Select Train a model and choose This computer, or a registered Linux worker. Load the example inputs, then select the Python environment containing your training libraries. Review the number of epochs, image size, batch size and device. Run workflow submits a real background job. Select the job to inspect its status and result, and use Read selected logs when you need details. Successful vision training produces a checkpoint, an ONNX model, preprocessing information and calibration data. Check held out results before choosing a model; a completed job alone does not establish useful accuracy.

title: Optimise and compile
text: Optimise with bounded trials compares a limited set of training settings. Set a trial limit and use validation results to choose a candidate. Next, select Compile for Hailo. Supply the model's ONNX file and matching calibration data, and use a compatible Hailo compiler environment on Linux x86-64. The tested Hailo-8 and Hailo-8L path uses DFC 3.34. The Hailo-10H vision path uses DFC 5.4. We are reviewing compilation inputs here; the Mac does not run the vendor compiler natively. Successful compilation produces a target specific HEF file.

title: Package models and scripts
text: Select Package model and scripts after you have a compiled HEF. Enter the exact target and the Hailo runtime version installed on your Pi. Add a scripts directory and an entry point if your application needs them. The package records file hashes and deployment metadata. Keep preprocessing, labels and other required assets with the model. A preparation bundle from Build readiness is different: it describes the project and is not a compiled deployment model. Here we run packaging using the previously verified synthetic Hailo-8L HEF.

title: Add the bundle to an existing image
text: To distribute a customised operating system image, select Add bundle to an existing OS image. Supply an existing Raspberry Pi image and your deployment ZIP. The image workflow copies the source, adds the model and scripts, checks the filesystem, and writes a new image. It does not build a distribution or resize partitions. Use a base image with the correct runtime and enough space. Linux tools or the Docker backend perform the filesystem work. Raspberry Pi Imager is a separate final step: review the destination storage carefully before writing it.

title: Connect and test the Raspberry Pi
text: Open Enroll Pis and Linux workers to register a trusted SSH alias. Verify the Pi identity, accelerator and runtime before deployment. Back up the existing configuration and preserve the original service state. Select Upload and activate on Pi to deploy a reviewed package, then Test the Pi to run a bounded check. These controls are shown for preparation; this recording does not change your devices. Separate hardware tests completed on Raspberry Pi 5 (8GB), using the 13 TOPS Hailo-8L and 26 TOPS Hailo-8 AI HAT+ boards. Keep hardware execution and real model accuracy as separate checks.

title: Prepare a Hailo-10H language model project
text: For language models, create a Hailo-10H project and import reviewed instruction data. Prepare host recipe creates configuration; it does not start training. Actual fine tuning uses the Train a model workflow with a compatible local base model and the Transformers/PEFT engine. Hailo deployment has additional constraints. The supported vendor path starts with a Hailo provided pre optimised base archive and matching LoRA adapters. Arbitrary base models are not automatically convertible. Hailo's GenAI numerical emulator is unsupported, and final execution requires Hailo-10H hardware. Check the guide before committing to a model family.

title: Use the CLI and MCP interfaces
text: The native desktop, web interface, command line and MCP server are four ways to operate the same workbench. Use the command line for repeatable jobs with saved JSON specifications, and check logs and artifacts after each run. The MCP interface uses standard input and output for a connected assistant; it is not a public network endpoint. Always point each interface to the intended data directory. Start with a small end to end example, retain your evaluation evidence, and use the guide whenever a dependency or compatibility check fails.

title: Your next step
text: You are ready to create your first project, import reviewed data, and run a small training job. Then compile for the correct target, package the required assets, and test on the Pi with a verified recovery path. The guide and repository contain the full instructions. Thank you for watching.
